clue.text: O.T. judge had robe altered

indicators.note: altered says the letters of the words before it are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An Old Testament judge rearranged the robe he had on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' shuffles HAD and ROBE together; the clue's own words supply all seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Deborah was the prophetess who served as one of the judges of Israel in the Book of Judges.

clue.text: Assimilate effect of gravity in tides movements

indicators.note: in places the gravity letter inside the moved-about tides
movements says the letters of tides shift around into a new order

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Understanding how gravity drives the motion of the tides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movements' rearranges TIDES into DIEST, and 'in' places G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To digest information is to absorb it mentally, just as the body absorbs food.

clue.text: Well done, without publicity, to put on such a bold show

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the cheer goes around the advert

parts.note: bravo is a cry of approval meaning well done
an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: Praise for putting on a brave display without any advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. 'to put on' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a boastful display of courage meant to impress.

clue.text: Rigid metal rule

definitions.meaning: a stiff bar made of a hard element

explanation.surface: A stiff steel ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rule' looks like a measuring stick, but it is the second definition: tyranny.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron bar is literally a stiff metal stick, and to rule with one means to govern harshly.

clue.text: Head lock attendant

parts.note: read as wrestling it is a hold on the neck; read differently it is someone who tends the locks of the head

explanation.surface: A wrestling official who looks after holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head lock' is a wrestling hold, but here the locks are tresses on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon stylist cuts and styles tresses, so attends to the locks of one's head.

clue.text: The big prize for Marigold

parts.note: king as a prefix means big, as in king-size
a cup is a trophy awarded as a prize

explanation.surface: The top trophy goes to someone called Marigold.
explanation.walkthrough: Marigold looks like a person's name but is the flower. 'The' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingcup is the marsh marigold, a yellow buttercup-family flower of wet meadows.

clue.text: Used in part to spike gun barrel

indicators.note: used in part says only a portion of the following words is taken, a run straddling them

explanation.surface: Part of a soldier's kit for disabling a cannon.
explanation.walkthrough: To spike a gun was to drive a nail into its touch-hole; 'barrel' looks like the gun's, but is a cask.
explanation.definitionFit: A keg is a small cask, a barrel for beer.

clue.text: A blow with one's right, perhaps

definitions.text: A blow with one's right, perhaps

parts.words: A blow with one's right, perhaps
parts.note: a punch thrown with the right hand might land on the face's central feature, giving a slang name for that punch

explanation.surface: A boxer's punch thrown with the right hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The blow is named for where it lands, the hooter, not the hand that throws it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a punch on the snout, named for the body part it hits.

clue.text: The principal stock letter

definitions.meaning: chief or main, as an adjective
money invested, the funds of a business

explanation.surface: The headmaster's share certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions run together: principal (adjective), stock (funds) and letter (upper case).
explanation.definitionFit: Capital means chief, also wealth invested, and also an upper-case letter.

clue.text: Skittish sort of writer ?

parts.note: skittish usually means nervous or frisky, but here it means given to writing skits, comic imitations

explanation.surface: A nervous, flighty author.
explanation.walkthrough: Skittish is read as 'skit-ish': someone who writes skits, i.e. comic imitations.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a burlesque imitation, so its writer is a satirist who mimics other works.

clue.text: What a keeper should do for circus security ?

definitions.text: What a keeper should do for circus security ?

parts.words: What a keeper should do for circus security
parts.note: a keeper at a circus would watch over the arena; a keeper is also a ring worn to stop another ring slipping off a finger

explanation.surface: Advice on how a zookeeper protects the big top's arena.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase read as an instruction says to protect the circus arena; as a noun it names the jeweller's keeper ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper ring is a band worn above a wedding ring to hold it in place, so its job is protection.

clue.text: Extra splendid

definitions.meaning: an extra in a film is a supernumerary, a walk-on actor

explanation.surface: Something especially wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: A film extra is a super (short for supernumerary), and super is also slang for excellent.

clue.text: " The very — of my age, my very prop " (Mer of Venice)

definitions.text: " The very — of my age, my very prop " (Mer of Venice)

parts.words: The very — of my age, my very prop
parts.note: Old Gobbo's line in The Merchant of Venice about his son Launcelot; the missing word is a support, matching prop

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the blank from the quotation; 'my very prop' points to a walking stick that supports an old man.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking stick or supporting pole is what an aged person leans on, hence prop.

clue.text: Cleaned tar up the wrong way indeed!

indicators.note: in, split off from indeed, puts the turned-round words inside the following word

parts.note: a deed is an act or something done

indicators.note: the wrong way says the words tar and up are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cleaned the tarmac by the odd method of doing it backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' splits into 'in deed': PURAT (TAR UP turned round by 'the wrong way') goes inside DEED, split DE...ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To depurate is to purify or free from impurities, an old word for clean.

clue.text: What a long face!

parts.note: read as an exclamation it comments on a gloomy look; read literally it is a lengthy word for a face

explanation.surface: A remark on someone's miserable expression.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the word meaning face is itself very long, eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Physiognomy means the features or countenance of a person.

clue.text: Do such polite addresses — proverbially cost nothing?

definitions.text: Do such polite addresses — proverbially cost nothing?

parts.words: Do such polite addresses — proverbially cost nothing
parts.note: the proverb says that politeness costs nothing; the courteous forms of address are honorific ranks given to peers' children

explanation.surface: A question whether polite forms of address are free, as the saying goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'courtesy costs nothing'; the phrase wanted is the honorifics such as 'Lord' or 'Lady' borne by a peer's children by custom, not by right.
explanation.definitionFit: Honorifics used for a duke's or earl's children are styles granted out of politeness rather than law.

clue.text: In double trouble about a partner that's lacking spirit 9>-

indicators.note: about means the stirred letters go around the clue's a
trouble means the doubled letters are stirred up into a new order
double means the word in is taken twice over

parts.note: taken as written
a mate is a partner or spouse

explanation.surface: Someone in serious difficulty over a partner with no spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' gives ININ, 'trouble' rearranges it as INNI, and 'about' wraps that round A to make INANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inanimate has no life or soul, being without animating spirit.

clue.text: Told story of a shipping line

parts.note: to spin a tale is to tell one
a yarn is a long tale

explanation.surface: Someone recounted a tale about a shipping company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipping line' suggests a shipping company, but means a rope used aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Spunyarn is a light cord of twisted rope-yarns used for seizing on board ship.

clue.text: He forecasts a giant root-crops output

indicators.note: output means what the words are turned into, a reworking of their letters

explanation.surface: A huge root vegetable harvest is predicted by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'output' rearranges GIANT and ROOT-CROPS; the 'a' before 'giant' is a link word, not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosticator is one who predicts the future, a soothsayer or forecaster.

clue.text: Means of bringing travellers to book

definitions.meaning: a public road vehicle carrying passengers, the old full name for a bus

explanation.surface: A coach that brings tourists to a library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The full old name for a bus, and also a single volume that reprints several works by one author.

clue.text: Ancient MS reveals an experienced worker

parts.note: old means ancient
MS stands for manuscript, a handwritten document, so a hand

explanation.surface: An old manuscript shows a veteran's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reveals' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long practice at a job.

clue.text: Former nurse is put out

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to tend is to look after, as a nurse does

explanation.surface: A one-time nurse is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like annoyed, but means stretch out.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a hand is to stretch it forth.

clue.text: " … a cook and a captain bold, And the mate of the ——" (Gilbert)

definitions.text: " … a cook and a captain bold, And the mate of the ——" (Gilbert)

parts.words: … a cook and a captain bold, And the mate of the ——
parts.note: W. S. Gilbert's Bab Ballad The Yarn of the Nancy Bell, whose sole survivor claims to be every member of a ship's crew

explanation.surface: A line from a comic ballad by W. S. Gilbert with the ship's name left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is 'The Yarn of the Nancy Bell'; the survivor says he is the cook, the captain, the mate and the crew of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation names a two-masted sailing vessel called the Nancy.

clue.text: For whom the heir of Redclyffe succeeded

definitions.text: For whom the heir of Redclyffe succeeded

parts.words: For whom the heir of Redclyffe succeeded
parts.note: The Heir of Redclyffe is an 1853 Victorian bestseller; its success was the author's, Charlotte Mary

explanation.surface: Asking whose estate the heir inherited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heir' and 'succeeded' suggest inheritance, but the novel succeeded for its author, Charlotte M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist Charlotte Mary wrote The Heir of Redclyffe, her greatest success.

clue.text: A pointer to what books not to read

definitions.meaning: a forefinger or a needle on a dial points the way
the Catholic Church's list of prohibited books

explanation.surface: A guide steering readers away from forbidden books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The forefinger is the pointing digit, and the Vatican's former list banned certain books from Catholic readers.

clue.text: Vestment taken by an early saint

indicators.note: taken by places the clue's an after the vestment, as if carried along behind it

parts.note: an alb is a white linen vestment worn by priests
taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest's robe was carried off by a saint in the early church.
explanation.walkthrough: St Alban is Britain's first recorded Christian martyr.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban was a Romano-British martyr, venerated as Britain's first saint.

clue.text: Make more of a stage jewel

parts.note: a prop is a stage property, an object used by actors
an agate is a semi-precious gemstone

explanation.surface: Getting extra value out of a theatrical gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a stage' reads as a noun phrase, but stage qualifies the missing word: a stage property.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate is to breed or multiply plants or animals, producing more of them.

clue.text: Dog fox is a fighter

definitions.meaning: a small snub-nosed breed of dog
an old dialect name for a fox, used in hunting

explanation.surface: A dog that fights foxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the dog breed, a hunting name for the fox, and a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a small flat-faced dog, the fox was once so called, and a boxer is short for pugilist.

clue.text: Financial reserve of China, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: savings set aside for the future
a porcelain egg left in a hen's nest to encourage laying

explanation.surface: A question about China's state savings.
explanation.walkthrough: China with a capital looks like the country but is porcelain: a dummy egg of china placed in a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings kept by are named after the decoy egg placed in a hen's box to induce laying.

clue.text: Gave in, twitched an eyelid, and died

indicators.note: twitched says the letters of the word next to it jerk into a new order

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies and records

explanation.surface: A person surrendered, flickered an eye and expired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twitched' rearranges EYELID into YIELDE, then D for died finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in is to surrender or submit, the same as to concede.
